sections.title: 一、詞彙（10分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第1至10題，每題選出一個最適當的選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯或劃記多於一個選項者倒扣1/3分，倒扣到本大題之實得分數為零為止。未作答者，不給分亦不扣分。

questions.stem: With his excellent social skills, Steven has been ______ as a great communicator by all his colleagues.
When you enter a building, be sure to look behind you and hold the door open for someone coming through the same door. It is a common ______ in many cultures.
The telephone has changed beyond ______ in recent years. In both form and function, it has become totally different from what it was before.
Though Jack has moved out of his parents’ house, he is ______ dependent on them still. They send him a check every month for his living expenses.
If you want to keep your computer from being attacked by new viruses, you need to constantly renew and ______ your anti-virus software.
Many factors may explain why people are addicted to the Internet. One factor ______ to this phenomenon is the easy access to the Net.
We were ______ awaiting the results of the school’s annual English drama contest. Our class won the first place last year, and we certainly wanted to win again this year.
Tropical rainforests are home to about one million plant and animal species. If the rainforests disappear, many of these species will become ______.
An honest person is faithful to his promise. Once he makes a ______, he will not go back on his own word.
The new computer game Wii provides us with an ______ way of exercising. People now may play sports in their living rooms, which was unimaginable before.

sections.title: 三、文意選填（10分）
sections.instructions: 說明：第31至40題，每題一個空格。請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項中分別選出最適當者，並將其字母代號標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯或劃記多於一個選項者倒扣1/9分，倒扣到本大題之實得分數為零為止。未作答者，不給分亦不扣分。

A trip to the supermarket has now become an exercise in psychological warfare. Shopkeepers know that filling a store with the smell of freshly baked bread makes people feel hungry and [[31]] them to buy more food than they intended. Stocking the most [[32]] products at eye level helps them sell faster than cheaper but less visible competitors.
Researchers on customer behavior are now investigating how “swarm intelligence” (that is, how social animals like ants or bees behave in a crowd) can be used to [[33]] what people buy. The idea is that, if a certain product is seen to be popular, shoppers are [[34]] to choose it too. With the help of modern technology, some supermarkets are now able to keep customers [[35]] about what others are buying. As a customer walks past a shelf of goods in one of these supermarkets, a screen on the shelf will tell him how many people currently in the store have chosen that particular [[36]]. As it turns out, such a “swarm moves” model [[37]] sales without the need to give people discounts. The reason is simple: it gives shoppers the [[38]] of knowing that they bought the “right” product—that is, the one everyone else bought.
The psychology that works in physical stores is just as [[39]] on the Internet. Online retailers such as Amazon are good at telling shoppers which products are popular with like-minded consumers. Even in the [[40]] of your home, you can still be part of the swarm.

Japan is dealing with a problem that’s just starting to sweep the world—an aging population combined with a shrinking work force. [[41]] By so doing, it is hoped that Japan’s government will save its increasingly burdened pension (i.e., payment received after retirement) system from going bankrupt. In 2000, the Japanese could get a full pension from the government at 60. [[42]] What’s more, premiums paid by workers every month are set to rise while payouts they get after retirement fall.
To help workers to cope with this, Japan passed a law last year that requires companies by 2013 to raise their retirement age from 60 to 65 or rehire their retired workers. [[43]] In a country where forced layoffs are a last resort, large companies traditionally have relied on retirement to reduce payrolls. They were just about to enjoy a big cut in personnel costs because of the mass retirement of Japan’s baby boomers. [[44]] Consequently, there was much opposition from corporations to the new retirement law. Early signs suggest that large corporations will hesitate in raising their retirement ages. [[45]] Violators of the new law would face only “administrative guidance,” not penalties. Such resistance is hurting the effectiveness of the policies, which may thus prolong the aging problem.

sections.title: 五、閱讀測驗（22分）
sections.instructions: 說明：第46至56題，每題請分別根據各篇文章的文意選出一個最適當的選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得2分，答錯或劃記多於一個選項者倒扣2/3分，倒扣到本大題之實得分數為零為止。未作答者，不給分亦不扣分。

groups.passage:
Andrew Carnegie, once the world’s richest person, was born in 1835 to a weaver’s family in Scotland. As a child, he was expected to follow his father’s profession. But the industrial revolution destroyed the weavers’ craft, and the family had to leave for new possibilities in America.
In 1848 the Carnegies arrived in Pittsburgh, then the iron-manufacturing center of the country. Young Carnegie took odd jobs at a cotton factory and later worked as a messenger boy in the telegraph office. He was often asked to deliver messages to the city theater, where he would stay to watch plays by great playwrights. He also spent most of his leisure hours in a small library that a local benefactor made available to working boys.
After the Civil War, Carnegie saw great potential in the iron industry. He devoted himself to the replacement of wooden bridges with stronger iron ones and earned a fortune. He further introduced a new steel refining process to convert iron into steel. By 1900, Carnegie Steel produced more of the metal than all of Great Britain.
However, Carnegie often expressed his uneasiness with the businessman’s life. Wishing to spend more time receiving instruction and reading systematically, he once wrote, “To continue much longer overwhelmed by business cares and with most of my thoughts wholly upon the way to make more money in the shortest time, must degrade me beyond hope of permanent recovery.” The strong desire for intellectual pursuit led him to sell his company and retire at 64.
Fond of saying that “the man who dies rich dies disgraced,” Carnegie then turned his attention to giving away his fortune. He abhorred charity; instead, he used his money to help others help themselves. He established over 2,500 public libraries, and sponsored numerous cultural, educational and scientific institutions. By the time he died in 1919, he had given away 350 million dollars.

groups.passage:
Most parents dread a note or call from school saying that their child’s behavior is “not normal.” If your child’s academic performance and social life is suffering because they don’t pay attention, can’t sit still and act without thinking, it is most likely that they have AD/HD (Attention Deficit/ Hyperactivity Disorder).
AD/HD is a neurological disorder which stems not from the home environment, but from biological and genetic causes. Its symptoms typically show up in early childhood. The main characteristics are inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity. Inattentive children have difficulty focusing on completing a task or learning something new. Hyperactive children always seem to be restless. Often they report that they need to stay busy and may try to do several tasks at once. Impulsive children often do not think before they act. They often blurt out inappropriate comments or have difficulty taking turns in conversation.
Most children can be inattentive, hyperactive, or impulsive at times. It is when these behaviors are inappropriate for their age and affect different areas in their lives that the disorder is diagnosed. Depression, anxiety, and learning disabilities may co-exist with AD/HD. Therefore, if a child is suspected of AD/HD, it is very important that he or she be evaluated by a professional.
Once your child is diagnosed with AD/HD, it is important to let the school know so that they can provide appropriate academic and social support. Your child’s school should keep this information confidential and it can usually make accommodations in the classroom to fit your child’s learning needs.

groups.passage:
Conflict diamonds, sometimes called blood diamonds, are diamonds that are sold to fund the unlawful and illegal operations of rebel, military and terrorist groups. Countries that have been most affected by conflict diamonds are Sierra Leone, Angola, Liberia and the Democratic Republic of Congo. They are places where citizens have been terrorized or even killed by groups in control of the local diamond trade.
Wars in most of those areas have ended or at least decreased in intensity, but the problem of conflict diamonds hasn’t gone away. Diamonds mined in some rebel-held areas, such as Liberia, are being smuggled into neighboring countries and exported as conflict-free diamonds.
In order to stop blood diamond sales, South African countries with a legitimate diamond trade began a campaign in 2000 to track the origins of all rough diamonds. Their efforts resulted in the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme (KPCS), an international organization to make the world free of conflict diamonds. The goals of the KPCS are to document and track all rough diamonds when they enter a participating country. Shippers are required to place those diamonds in sealed boxes and provide enough detailed information about their origins to prove they did not originate in a conflict zone.
It’s difficult for most of us to imagine what life is like in countries where diamonds are the source of so much chaos and suffering. Furthermore, the connection between terror and diamonds is not something that’s reported heavily in the press. The 2006 movie Blood Diamond, starring Leonardo DiCaprio, should help make the issue more mainstream, if only temporarily. So, take some time to learn more about the problems that conflict diamonds create, and then follow your heart the next time you shop for a diamond.

questions.label: 英文翻譯1
questions.stem: 大眾運輸的快速發展已逐漸縮短了都市和鄉村的距離。

96指考英文考科非選擇題分為兩部份（佔28分）：一、英文翻譯（8分）；二、英文作文（20分）。英文翻譯評分原則，乃依語法與用字評分；英文作文則分內容（5分）、組織（5分）、文法與句構（4分）、字彙與拼字（4分）、體例（2分）等五項評分（參閱表1）。

以下非選擇題各大題之參考答案以及評分標準的說明，乃依據「九十六學年度指定科目考試人工閱卷英文考科評分標準訂定會議」彙整而成，以供各界參考。英文作文部分，提供評分標準，請參考。至於各等級之評分樣例，可參閱選才通訊第142期「學測與指考英文作文評分樣例」說明（http://www.ceec.edu.tw/CeecMag/articles/142-2.htm），該文以93年學測與指考英文作文為題所作之評分樣例。

本題型在於測驗考生根據中文提示，運用適當之英文詞彙、句型與語法表情達意的能力。第一句評量考生使用高中常用詞彙（如：development, transportation, gradually, shorten, distance等）及基本句型（如：現在完成式）的能力。

sections.title: 二、英文作文（20分）
sections.instructions:
說明：1. 依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2. 文長至少120個單詞。

questions.label: 英文作文
questions.stem: 提示：你能想像一個沒有電(electricity)的世界嗎？請寫一篇文章，第一段描述我們的世界沒有了電以後，會是甚麼樣子，第二段說明這樣的世界是好是壞，並舉例解釋原因。
questions.scoring_notes:
96指考英文考科非選擇題分為兩部份（佔28分）：一、英文翻譯（8分）；二、英文作文（20分）。英文翻譯評分原則，乃依語法與用字評分；英文作文則分內容（5分）、組織（5分）、文法與句構（4分）、字彙與拼字（4分）、體例（2分）等五項評分（參閱表1）。

以下非選擇題各大題之參考答案以及評分標準的說明，乃依據「九十六學年度指定科目考試人工閱卷英文考科評分標準訂定會議」彙整而成，以供各界參考。英文作文部分，提供評分標準，請參考。至於各等級之評分樣例，可參閱選才通訊第142期「學測與指考英文作文評分樣例」說明（http://www.ceec.edu.tw/CeecMag/articles/142-2.htm），該文以93年學測與指考英文作文為題所作之評分樣例。

評分標準：
本大題總分20分，主要評量考生是否有能力撰寫一篇語法正確、語意通順，並且內容統一、組織連貫的英文作文。
採整體式評分，分為五等級：特優（19-20分）、優（15-18分）、可（10-14分）、差（5-9分）、劣（0-4分），閱卷委員於閱讀完考生試卷後，於腦海裡產生一個分數，再以各分項評分標準（請見表1）檢閱是否符合整體印象分數。另外，字數明顯不足，扣1分。未分段，扣1分；寫三段，不扣分。不一定要使用假設語氣，只要整篇時態一致，內容切合題意，就不扣分。

表1：英文作文分項式評分指標（等級：優／可／差／劣）
內容｜優：主題(句)清楚切題，並有具體、完整的相關細節支持。(5-4分)｜可：主題不夠清楚或突顯，部分相關敘述發展不全。(3分)｜差：主題不明，大部分相關敘述發展不全或與主題無關。(2-1分)｜劣：文不對題或沒寫（凡文不對題或沒寫者，其他各項均以零分計算）。(0分)
組織｜優：重點分明，有開頭、發展、結尾，前後連貫，轉承語使用得當。(5-4分)｜可：重點安排不妥，前後發展比例與轉承語使用欠妥。(3分)｜差：重點不明、前後不連貫。(2-1分)｜劣：全文毫無組織或未按提示寫作。(0分)
文法、句構｜優：全文幾無文法錯誤，文句結構富變化。(4分)｜可：文法錯誤少，且未影響文意之表達。(3分)｜差：文法錯誤多，且明顯影響文意之表達。(2-1分)｜劣：全文文法錯誤嚴重，導致文意不明。(0分)
字彙、拼字｜優：用字精確、得宜，且幾無拼字錯誤。(4分)｜可：字詞單調、重複，用字偶有不當，少許拼字錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。(3分)｜差：用字、拼字錯誤多，明顯影響文意之表達。(2-1分)｜劣：只寫出或抄襲與題意有關的零碎字詞。(0分)
體例｜優、可（合併欄）：格式、標點、大小寫幾無錯誤。(2分)｜差：格式、標點、大小寫等有錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。(1分)｜劣：違背基本的寫作體例或格式，標點、大小寫等錯誤甚多。(0分)

註2：96指考英文科閱卷籌備會議資料，改編自張武昌等（民93）「英文寫作能力測驗規劃研究（VI）」研究報告。台北：大考中心。

tags.topic: a world without electricity: what it would be like and whether it is good or bad

extraction.method: Word 版 paper-2.doc（soffice 轉 docx + python-docx）為主文字來源，pdftotext -layout／-raw 擷取 paper-1.pdf 逐字比對，並以 Read 逐頁檢視題本 PDF 全部 8 頁頁面影像核對；選擇題答案取自 answer.pdf（多科合併，只取「英文考科選擇題參考答案」頁，pdftotext）；英文翻譯參考答案與作文評分表取自 scoring.pdf（選才通訊第156期文章，第3–5頁為英文部分），以 Read 檢視頁面影像並以 pdftoppm 250dpi 放大大括號樹狀圖人工轉寫；統計以 xlrd 讀取 stats-1.xls、stats-2.xls 英文科工作表（工作表「2」），並與官方答案交叉核對。；查證者（verifier）獨立重做：soffice 重新轉 Word 版並逐題比對題幹、選項、選文（含 [[題號]] 位置與段落），pdftotext -raw 逐段比對與字數核對，Read 檢視題本 PDF 全部頁面、answer.pdf 英文頁、scoring.pdf 第3–5頁（翻譯樹狀圖以 250dpi 放大），xlrd 重新讀 stats-1／stats-2 全部 56 題逐欄比對。
issues: 結構與 gsat-spec.json legacy_ast「94–97」期別完全一致：詞彙 1–10（10×1，4選項）、綜合測驗 11–30（4篇×5題×1＝20）、文意選填 31–40（(A)–(J) 10選項，10×1）、篇章結構 41–45（(A)–(E) 5選項，5×2）、閱讀測驗 46–56（3篇：46–49、50–52、53–56，11題×2＝22）、英文翻譯 2題（評分標準：每小題滿分4分，共8分）、英文作文 20分（文長至少120個單詞）；第壹部分選擇題 72分、第貳部分非選擇題 28分，合計 100；封面印考試時間 80 分鐘。本年有倒扣（詞彙／綜合 1/3、文意選填 1/9、篇章結構 1/2、閱讀 2/3），各大題說明已逐字保留。
題號重複警告（validator: 題號重複 [1, 2]）是刻意的：英文翻譯在題本中編為 1.、2.，作文沒有題號；validator 要求 no 必須是整數，因此翻譯用 no=1、2（label「英文翻譯1」「英文翻譯2」，本年大題名稱為「英文翻譯」而非「中譯英」），作文用 no=1（label「作文」），label 皆不重複。做法與 ast-98、ast-99 相同。

說明文字的冒號照題本：詞彙、綜合測驗的說明用「說明︰」（U+FE30），文意選填、篇章結構、閱讀、英文翻譯、英文作文用「說明：」（U+FF1A），Word 版與 PDF 文字層一致。英文翻譯、作文說明在題本中為兩行（1.／2.），以換行分隔。各題組前的「第 11 至 15 題為題組」等標題（PDF 頁面影像為「爲」字）沒有放進 JSON（schema 沒有對應欄位）。英文翻譯說明只有「未按題意翻譯者，不予計分」，題本未印每題配分；每題4分取自評分標準。

文字來源與核對：選文、題幹、選項以 Word 版（paper-2.doc）為主，再以 pdftotext -raw 對 paper-1.pdf 逐段比對（237 段文字去除空白後全部吻合，只差頁首頁尾與中文斷行），並以 Read 逐頁檢視 PDF 全部 8 頁頁面影像。選文段落以空行（\n\n）分隔；Word 版在第27、45題空格後有軟換行（PDF 頁面影像中下一行頂格、沒有縮排，屬同一段），已併回同一段。Word 版第6題 (D)、第13題 (C)、第53題 (A) 選項尾端多餘空格已去除。第21–25題組的溫度符號照 Word／PDF 文字層寫成「1° F」「2° to 6° F」（U+00B0，PDF 影像為上標小圓圈）。

題本原文照錄未改：第16–20題組首句「The northern lights, ... is one of nature’s most dazzling spectacles.」（複數主詞配 is）；第50–52題組「their child’s academic performance and social life is suffering」與「AD/HD (Attention Deficit/ Hyperactivity Disorder)」（斜線後有空格）；第7題「Our class won the first place last year」。
題本格式未保留（依 schema 不保留粗斜體）：第53–56題組選文與第55題 (B) 的片名 Blood Diamond 為斜體。本卷沒有問畫底線字的題目，也沒有圖表。
英文翻譯第1題：評分標準 PDF 引用的題目為「大眾運輸的快速發展已經逐漸縮短了都市和鄉村的距離。」（多一個「經」字），題本與 Word 版皆為「已逐漸縮短」，stem 以題本為準。參考答案樹狀圖中「cities and countries.」照原圖照錄（依中文「鄉村」語意應為 countryside，但官方原文如此，未更正）。

英文翻譯參考答案在評分標準 PDF（選才通訊第156期文章第4頁）中是大括號樹狀圖，以 pdftoppm 250dpi 放大逐格轉寫，完整轉寫放在 scoring_notes（以 [ ] 表示一個大括號）。answer 為每個括號取第一個選項組成的一句：第2題「Rail(way)」取 Rail、「in/within」取 in；原圖以大圓括號括住的 system／network／link／Service 一欄（依註1「( )（括弧）表示該字詞可省略」）保留第一項 system。accepted_answers 以斜線列出同位置可替換字詞，前後有空格的「 / 」表示整個片語替換；Service 在原圖中首字大寫，照錄。v1.1：兩題已依原圖填 answer_segments，answer_is_composite 為 true（官方只印樹狀圖、沒有印整句）；第1題「(the) urban and (the) rural areas.」展開為 urban and rural areas.／the urban and rural areas.／the urban and the rural areas. 三種（只省略前一個 the 的「urban and the rural areas」不通順，未列入）；第2題 Rail(way) 展開為 Rail／Railway，in/within 拆成兩個寫法；可省略的 system／network／link／Service 一欄只接在有冠詞的 the High-Speed Rail／the High-Speed Railway 之後（與「不接」合為同一段的 10 種寫法），沒有冠詞的 high-speed rail／high-speed railway／HSR 只收不接名詞的寫法——「With high-speed railway network」「With HSR system」這類可數名詞缺冠詞的組合不通順，未列入（原圖各欄獨立排列，accepted_answers 與 scoring_notes 的原圖轉寫照舊）。

作文：評分標準表1 的體例列為優、可兩欄合併（格式、標點、大小寫幾無錯誤。(2分)），差、劣各一欄，scoring_notes 照圖轉寫並註明合併欄。評分說明另有「寫三段，不扣分。不一定要使用假設語氣，只要整篇時態一致，內容切合題意，就不扣分。」已逐字收錄。官方未公布範文，answer 為 null。評分標準 PDF 中作文提示的括號為全形「（electricity）」，stem 以題本半形「(electricity)」為準。

統計：答對率 P、高分組 Ph、低分組 Pl、鑑別度 D 取自 stats-1.xls 英文科工作表（工作表「2」，報考 100,059、缺考 4,953、到考 95,106）；option_rates 取自 stats-2.xls 選項分析的「T」（全體）列，未含「未答」比例，所以各題 option_rates 加總小於 1（未答最高為第18題 25%）。stats-1 的五等組 Pa–Pe、D1–D4 與 stats-2 的高／低分組各選項比例（H／L 列）沒有放入（schema 無對應欄位）。本年沒有非選擇題得分分布檔，翻譯與作文的 stats 填 null。

統計交叉核對：56 題選項分析標「*」的選項與 answer.pdf 官方答案全部一致；兩檔只有兩處差 1 個百分點：第38題高分組（stats-1 Ph 73、stats-2 H 列 * 選項 74），第39題答對率（stats-1 P 27、stats-2 T 列 (A)* 28），推測為四捨五入差異。correct_rate／high_group 以 stats-1 為準，option_rates 照 stats-2，因此第39題 option_rates.A＝0.28 與 correct_rate＝0.27 不同。另第1題（D＝0.02，P＝0.30，(D) concerned 選答 31% 多於正答）與第15題（P＝0.12，D＝0.07，(C) before 選答 32%）鑑別度極低，數值已與原始檔再次核對無誤。
答案檔 answer.pdf 為數學乙、國文、英文等多科合併，只取「英文考科選擇題參考答案」頁。

標註判斷說明：第13題 After that、第17題 At other times（與前句 Sometimes 呼應）標 connective／phrase；第14題 later in life、第23題 Indirectly（呼應 both directly and indirectly）、第25題 less probable 依上下文邏輯判斷，標 discourse；第19題 takes place 為敘述一般事實用現在簡單式，標 grammar/tense；第30題 with + 受詞 + 過去分詞（with foreign influences and tourism regulated）標 grammar/participle；第32題由後文 than cheaper but less visible competitors 對比判斷，標 discourse。篇章結構：第41題 B 以 Therefore 承接人口老化問題，且下一句 By so doing 回指 B 的 work longer，標 transition_word；第42題 D 以 But 與前句 In 2000 ... at 60 對比，標 contrast；第43題 A 為下文（企業依賴退休縮減人事成本）的主題句，標 topic_sentence；第44題 E 的 These people 指 baby boomers，標 pronoun_reference；第45題 C 以 And 追加企業敢於延遲的理由（與後句 Violators ... only administrative guidance 並列），標 transition_word。第41–45題組 genre 標 news（報導日本去年通過的退休年齡法案）。

查證（verifier）：56 題答案與 answer.pdf 英文頁（文字層與頁面影像）逐題一致；全部選項、題幹、選文與 Word 版逐字一致，並與 PDF 文字層逐段吻合；9 篇選文首句、末句、段落數（1/2/2/2/3/2/5/4/4）與字數（133/117/129/118/240/204/314/255/289，不計空格題號）皆與 PDF 一致；本卷無圖表；56 題 P／Ph／Pl／D 與 option_rates 全部與 stats-1、stats-2 相符，原解析者所述第38、39題 1 個百分點差異屬實；翻譯參考答案樹狀圖、作文評分表與評分說明逐字核對無誤。未發現需要更正之處。
